title: quest task list answers about the checked-out branch while the before-you-report-clear rule asks about the repository, and an empty list reads as the check passing
description:
Reported by opum-doc 2026-09-15, reproduced here. THE REPORT UNDERSTATES IT: this repository already decided this exact question once, in the opposite direction, and built the machinery -- `task list` simply never inherited it.

THE REPORTED SHAPE. The opum-sdlc skill says to run `quest task list --status "In Progress"`, read rather than remembered, before a session reports itself clear -- precisely because deferred closes go missing. opum-doc ran it on `dev` right after a merge. It returned EMPTY while ODOC-215 was In Progress with an open PR #300, because `.quest/tasks/ODOC-215.json` exists only on an unmerged branch:

  git cat-file -e origin/dev:.quest/tasks/ODOC-215.json        -> absent
  git show origin/docs/ODOC-215-...:.quest/tasks/ODOC-215.json -> ODOC-215 | In Progress

Reproduced in this repository within the hour, with the same shape: QCLI-315 was filed on chore/tracker-notes-307-313-314 and `git cat-file -e origin/dev:.quest/tasks/QCLI-315.json` fails. Any session on `dev` asking what is open cannot see it.

THE OBJECT MISMATCH, which is the defect and not the branch-scoping. The rule asks "is anything open in this REPOSITORY"; the command answers "is anything open on this BRANCH"; and the two diverge for exactly the tasks most likely to be forgotten -- the ones still on an unmerged branch. The failure direction is the bad one: an empty list reads as THE CHECK PASSING rather than as THE CHECK NOT RUNNING.

WHY THE REPORT UNDERSTATES IT. opum-doc wrote "branch-scoped is the only coherent behaviour for a git-backed tracker" and asked only for a footer saying which object was answered about. But QCLI-279 already rejected working-tree-only as the right object for a repository-wide question, for id allocation, and called the consequence a silent duplicate -- reproduced three times on its own filing. The fix it shipped is `highestSequenceOnOtherRefs` in src/cli/main.ts: `listRefs` + `listFiles` per ref, a tree listing per ref and never a history walk, degrading to today's behaviour when there is no Git repository. Measured: that function has exactly one caller, id allocation. `task list` reads the working tree alone.

So the machinery exists, its cost is already understood and accepted on a hotter path (every task creation), and the precedent for "a question about the repository must consult refs" is already set in this codebase. That changes the available fixes: a footer is the floor, not the ceiling.

RELATED, SAME ROOT, DIFFERENT SURFACE, found here two hours earlier: opum-agent swept origin/dev for a promotion-guard task, found none in quest-cli, and directed one be filed -- QCLI-314 already existed on its implementing branch. A task filed on the branch that implements it is invisible to an origin/dev search for the whole in-flight window, which is precisely the window in which a duplicate is most likely to be filed. That was reported as a hazard for a human/agent search; opum-doc's is the same root cause reaching an automated safety check. Two surfaces, one object mismatch.

DETECTION, worth keeping because neither exit codes nor output would have shown it: opum-doc did not trust the empty list, because an independent source (they had been told ODOC-215 was In Progress) disagreed with it. `gh pr list` is the cheap independent source. Checking an outcome against something other than the command's own success is the only thing that catches a check which passes by not looking.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An empty or filtered task list cannot be read as a repository-wide answer: the command states which object it answered about, naming the branch, and says that other refs may carry task records

The decision names WHICH of three options was taken and why, rather than treating this as branch-scoped vs refs-aware: (a) a footer naming the branch only, (b) a cross-ref EXISTENCE notice built on filenames alone -- the same tree listing highestSequenceOnOtherRefs already does -- or (c) a cross-ref READ. The allocator precedent must be addressed explicitly, including the asymmetry that makes it NOT extend for free: it needs only filenames and max-over-integers, which is commutative and cannot disagree with itself, while a cross-ref read of status needs git show plus a JSON parse per record per ref AND a policy for when two refs carry the same id with different statuses. Option (c) therefore invents a merge policy for tracker state, which is a larger decision than this ticket.
Proven both ways as two runs: a task record present only on an unmerged branch, and one present on the checked-out branch, with the command's output read in each case rather than its exit code
The before-you-report-clear guidance names what an empty list is a claim about, wherever that guidance lives once this is settled

implementationNotes:
THE ALLOCATOR PRECEDENT DOES NOT EXTEND FOR FREE, and the reason is not cost. opum-doc found the asymmetry after withdrawing their "branch-scoped is the only coherent behaviour" universal, and it reshapes this task's second criterion rather than merely informing it.

VERIFIED HERE, not taken from their report -- they read my codebase from refs and described it exactly, and the clause that matters is one I had not drawn out myself:

  highestSequenceOnOtherRefs   src/cli/main.ts:741, sole caller nextTaskId at :791
  reads FILENAMES ONLY         name.slice(marker.length, name.length - ".json".length)
                               -> Number -> Math.max
  degrades                     catch { return 0 } with no Git

So the allocator's cross-ref operation is max-over-integers: commutative, order-independent, and INCAPABLE OF DISAGREEING WITH ITSELF. If two refs both carry QCLI-315.json, either answer is the same answer. That is why a tree listing suffices and why the operation is total.

`task list --status "In Progress"` cannot work that way, because status lives INSIDE the record. A cross-ref read needs `git show <ref>:<path>` plus a JSON parse per record per ref -- a different cost class, on a colder path -- and, far more importantly, it acquires a question the allocator provably does not have: WHEN TWO REFS CARRY THE SAME ID WITH DIFFERENT STATUSES, WHICH IS THE ANSWER? QCLI-315 is To Do on chore/tracker-notes-307-313-314 and will be Done on dev once that merges. A union reports a task simultaneously open and closed; a winner-picking rule has silently invented a MERGE POLICY FOR TRACKER STATE, which is a much larger decision than this ticket and does not belong inside it.

SO THERE ARE THREE OPTIONS, NOT TWO, and the middle one did not exist when this was filed:
  (a) FOOTER          name the branch. Cheapest, and only tells a reader the answer was
                      scoped; does not tell them whether the scoping mattered here.
  (b) EXISTENCE NOTICE  "0 In Progress on branch <name>. 3 task records exist on other refs
                      and were not read." Filenames only -- the SAME tree listing the
                      allocator already pays for -- no record read, no conflict policy.
                      Answers the question a safety check is actually asking: is my empty
                      list load-bearing?
  (c) CROSS-REF READ  a merged view. Needs the merge policy above.

(b) is opum-doc's proposal and is strictly more than a footer and strictly less than a merged view. Recorded as the leading candidate, NOT as the decision -- criterion 2 requires the choice to be made and reasoned, and whoever makes it should confirm the filename-only listing really does answer the safety question before adopting it, rather than taking that from this note.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, since this task's description says their report understated the defect. It did, and my correction then overstated the remedy: I wrote that the machinery exists and its cost is already accepted on a hotter path, which is true and which I let imply that reusing it was mostly a matter of deciding to. For (b) that implication holds. For (c) it does not, and (c) is what "consults refs as the allocator does" sounds like it means. The precedent transfers to the CHEAP half of the question and stops exactly where the record contents begin.

ONE PROPERTY OF THE ORIGINAL REPORT WORTH KEEPING, added by opum-doc afterwards: the check that returned the false all-clear was one they ran BECAUSE A SKILL TOLD THEM TO. The discipline is what produced the false confidence. A check performed out of habit is trusted more than an ad-hoc look, which is exactly backwards when the check answers about a narrower object than the rule intends.

THE EXISTENCE NOTICE MUST BE A SET DIFFERENCE, NOT A COUNT -- and measured here it is SILENT in the common case, which is a stronger property than opum-doc's own measurement showed.

They built the naive version by hand against their one non-dev ref and got 122 lines: every task record on that branch, essentially all of which dev already holds. Useless as a notice and worse than useless as a safety signal, because a session that sees 122 lines after an empty In Progress list learns nothing and stops reading it the second time. Subtracting what the current ref carries left exactly one line -- ODOC-215.json, the task the empty list had missed.

MEASURED HERE, 20 refs, and the ratio is far more extreme:
  records on the current ref (tasks/ + completed/ + archive/)   315
  raw ls-tree per ref                                           217-235 each, ~4,500 lines
  after the set difference                                      0 on EVERY ref

So on this repository the notice would print nothing at all. That is the property worth designing for: a notice that fires constantly is tuned out by its second appearance, while one that has been silent and then names a single id gets read. Its APPEARANCE is the signal. 122-to-1 shows the notice is readable; 4,500-to-0 shows it is quiet, and quiet is what makes it survive contact with a repository that has a lot of branches.

THEIR IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL, attributed rather than re-derived because they flagged it as the one thing they had not stated earlier: the subtrahend must span BOTH tasks/ and completed/. A record can sit in tasks/ on a branch and completed/ on dev, and comparing only tasks/ reports it as a phantom open task. Confirmed by construction here -- my measurement spanned tasks/, completed/ AND archive/, and every one of the 20 refs came back empty. Comparing only tasks/ against a repository with 80+ completed records would have produced phantom rows on every ref, which is how a silent notice becomes a noisy one and then an ignored one.

Still filenames only. Still one tree listing per ref. Still no conflict policy. The only addition to option (b) is the current ref's own listing as the subtrahend, which the caller already has in hand.

IMPLEMENTED as option (b), recorded as DEC-6. One correction to this record own analysis, and it is the reason criterion 2 asked for confirmation rather than adoption.

THE NOTE ABOVE PROVED THE WRONG HALF. It recorded ~4,500 raw rows collapsing to ZERO after the set difference across 20 refs, and read that as the property to design for. It is a real and useful measurement of QUIETNESS. It is also, on its own, indistinguishable from a notice that CANNOT FIRE -- which is the exact failure this repository caught in a CI gate earlier tonight, where a job went red for a deliberate violation and red again on the clean revert, and only the second run revealed the gate was broken.

MEASURED THE FIRING CASE, which nobody had: subtrahend origin/dev at 68b8471 (before PR #145), other ref the branch head 4374c69.
  ids on dev 313, ids on the branch 315
  difference: QCLI-315, QCLI-316 -- both To Do on that branch, both genuinely invisible from dev
So the notice is quiet AND sensitive, and only now is that measured rather than assumed. Re-measured the steady state today as well: 0 difference across all 20 refs, because every id on every live branch is also on dev.

THE REFINEMENT THE TASK DID NOT SPECIFY: the cross-ref read runs ONLY when the listing came back empty, while the branch name is stated on every listing. A non-empty list already tells the reader records exist and that this is a filtered view; an empty one is the case that reads as the check passing rather than the check not running, and is the only case where naming what was not read changes the conclusion. The ~180ms saving across 20 refs is real and is NOT the argument -- if it were, the honest move would be to pay it.

MUTATION MATRIX, naming WHICH test died:
  always read other refs (drop the empty-only guard)   5 pass / 2 fail   "goes quiet once merged" + "non-empty still names the object"
  subtrahend spans tasks/ only                         6 pass / 1 fail   "a task completed here is not a phantom", alone
  report every id, not the difference                  5 pass / 2 fail   "record on an unmerged branch is NAMED" + the phantom test
Each death matches the mutated property by name rather than incidentally, which is the QCLI-317 lesson applied: a mutant dying in a test whose name has nothing to do with the mutated line is a signal to open that test, not a pass.

THE PHANTOM TEST EXISTS BECAUSE MY FIRST TEST SET COULD NOT REACH IT. opum-doc flagged that the subtrahend must span tasks/, completed/ AND archive/tasks/, and my fixtures had no completed record, so mutant 2 would have survived a suite that looked thorough. A record sits in tasks/ on a branch and completed/ on dev once it is closed; a tasks/-only comparison names it as an unseen open task. Against 80+ completed records that fires on nearly every ref -- which is how a silent notice becomes a noisy one and then an ignored one.

Full check: 534 pass, 0 fail, exit 0.

CRITERION 4 IS SPLIT AND ONLY HALF IS MINE. quest help task list now states that a result, and an empty one especially, is a claim about the branch and not the repository, names the scope field and unseenTaskIds, and points at gh pr list as the independent cross-check -- which is the only thing that caught the original defect, since neither exit code nor output would ever have shown it. The corresponding before-you-report-clear rule lives in the opum-sdlc skill in opum-fleet, which I do not own; routed rather than edited. Left unchecked for that reason.

CRITERION 4 IS HALF DONE AND STAYS UNCHECKED, deliberately.

quest help task list now states that a result -- an empty one especially -- is a claim about the checked-out branch and not the repository, names the scope field and unseenTaskIds, and points at gh pr list as the independent cross-check. That last clause is the detection lesson from the original report rather than decoration: opum-doc caught the false all-clear only because an independent source disagreed with the empty list, and neither exit code nor output would ever have shown it.

The matching before-you-report-clear rule lives in the opum-sdlc skill, which ships from opum-fleet and which this repository does not own. Editing a peer governing file on my own initiative is the rail, not a convenience I am declining. Routed to opum-agent; left unchecked so nobody reads a half-done criterion as done.

A LIVE INSTANCE OF THIS TASK OWN DEFECT, from this session, worth recording because it is the same shape one level up. Minutes after landing the CLAUDE.md correction that source-gates fires per PUSH and the head commit decides, I told a peer I would not merge PR #149 until BOTH source-gates rows were green -- restating the belief I had just corrected, and attributing the row-counting rule to them. They do not count rows; they take newest-per-context.

Measured before merging: head fb08648 touches .quest/ and CLAUDE.md, neither in the watched path set, so no push run exists. Three workflow runs on that SHA, all pull_request, one source-gates row, mergeStateStatus CLEAN. The second row I said I would wait for was never going to arrive -- I would have hung on the very PR I wrote the rule about.

THE PART THAT GENERALISES, and it is this task subject exactly: MY WAITS WERE ALREADY CORRECT. gh pr checks --watch plus mergeStateStatus IS newest-per-context; nothing hung and nothing could have. Only the PROSE described a different algorithm than the tooling ran, and the prose is what travelled to a peer. A description of a method and the method are different objects, and the description is the one that gets relayed, believed, and repeated under someone else name. That is the same claim this task makes about task list -- the command answers about a narrower object than the rule intends -- with the description standing in for the command.
finalSummary:
quest task list read the checked-out ref .quest/ and nothing else while the rule that sends a session to it asks about the REPOSITORY, so an empty list read as the check passing rather than as the check not running. Landed as PR #149, squash-merged to dev as e9c3c62. Design call recorded as DEC-6.

SHIPPED: every task.list envelope carries an additive top-level scope {branch, otherRefsRead, unseenTaskIds?}. The branch is named on every listing; the cross-ref SET DIFFERENCE runs only when the listing came back empty, which is the only case where naming what was not read changes the reader conclusion. Existence only -- never status -- so it acquires no merge policy for tracker state. scope sits BEFORE principal and AFTER data: opum-cli-e2e confirmed that slot is bounded on both sides by two different assertions that fail on opposite edits, principal-last and contractVersion-at-index-1.

THE TASK OWN RECORDED EVIDENCE PROVED THE WRONG HALF, which is the finding worth more than the feature. The note measured ~4,500 raw rows collapsing to ZERO across 20 refs and read that as the property to design for. It proves the notice is QUIET and is, alone, indistinguishable from a notice that CANNOT FIRE -- the exact failure this repository caught in a CI gate the same night, where a job went red for a deliberate violation and red again on the clean revert. Measured the firing case, which nobody had: dev at 68b8471 against branch head 4374c69 yields exactly QCLI-315 and QCLI-316, out of 313 and 315 ids. Quiet AND sensitive, now measured rather than assumed.

VERIFIED as seven tests, plus a mutation matrix naming WHICH test died rather than counts: dropping the empty-only guard kills the two quietness tests; narrowing the subtrahend to tasks/ kills the phantom test alone; reporting every id instead of the difference kills the naming test and the phantom test. Each death matches the mutated property by name rather than incidentally. Full check 535 pass / 0 fail, exit 0.

THE PHANTOM TEST EXISTS BECAUSE MY FIRST FIXTURE SET COULD NOT REACH IT. opum-doc flagged that the subtrahend must span tasks/, completed/ AND archive/tasks/, and my fixtures held no completed record, so that mutant would have survived a suite that looked thorough.

CRITERION 4 IS HALF DONE AND LEFT UNCHECKED: the CLI-side guidance is in quest help task list; the matching skill-side rule lives in opum-fleet and was routed rather than edited, because editing a peer governing file on my own initiative is the rail.
